first.rationale: Shorter onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, while avoiding the margin, retention, and customer-quality risks that can accompany reactive discounting. Verify memory_86 for downstream revenue evidence and memory_73 for cohort quality and durability before final commitment.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. Verified evidence shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal. The test remains controlled because performance may vary in the current cohort and market context.
